steps.title: The promise
paragraphs: Ms Okafor holds up two essays. The first begins: “Uniforms are a topic many people talk about.”
The second begins: “Our school should drop uniforms because they cost families money, ignore the weather and stop students expressing themselves.”
“Which essay knows where it’s going?” she asks. Everyone points at the second.
“A thesis is a promise,” she says. “It tells me what you will prove, and the three reasons tell me what each body paragraph will be about.”

cards.title: Claim + because + reasons
cards.body: A strong argumentative thesis has a claim (what should happen) and the reasons that prove it: “[Topic] should [action] because [reason 1], [reason 2] and [reason 3].” Each reason becomes one body paragraph.

cards.title: Vague or specific?
cards.telling: Phones are a big issue in schools.
cards.showing: Schools should ban phones in class because they distract students, encourage cheating and cause conflict.
cards.note: “A big issue” promises nothing. The strong thesis takes a side and maps the essay.

cards.title: Check your thesis
cards.body: Could someone disagree? Is it one sentence? Does it name your reasons? Is it specific (not “good”, “bad” or “a big issue”)? Could you prove it with evidence?

prompts: Read one of your theses aloud. Could someone disagree with it?
Which reason in your thesis would make the strongest body paragraph?
